sources.title: Tanzil Quran Text (Uthmani, Version 1.1)
sources.author: Tanzil Project
sources.version: Version 1.1 (released February 2021); file downloaded 2026-10-22, copyright block dated 2007-2026
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0, with Tanzil's terms of use: verbatim copies only (changing the text is not allowed), the source (Tanzil Project) must be clearly indicated with a link to tanzil.net, and the copyright notice must be kept.
sources.credit: Quran text: Tanzil Project, Tanzil Quran Text (Uthmani, Version 1.1), CC BY 3.0, used verbatim. Check for updates at https://tanzil.net/
sources.notes: Downloaded from https://tanzil.net/pub/download/index.php with quranType=uthmani, outType=txt-2 (Text with aya numbers, 'sura|aya|text') and Tanzil's default options: pause marks on, sajdah signs on, rub-el-hizb signs off, tatweel below superscript alefs on, sequential tanweens off; agree=true. The raw file is kept verbatim in data/tanzil/quran-uthmani.txt and pinned by sha256 in scripts/fetch-quran.ts. data/quran.json stores each cited ayah as the NFC form of its line: for 34 of the 36 cited ayat NFC reorders combining marks (for example shadda after the vowel sign) or composes alef + madda into one code point. The result is canonically equivalent to the Tanzil line (same text under Unicode), not byte-identical. The Tanzil copyright block is kept verbatim in data/quran.json (meta.tanzilCopyright) and in LICENSES.

sources.title: The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (English translation), Tanzil file en.pickthall
sources.author: Mohammed Marmaduke William Pickthall
sources.license: Public domain: first published 1930; the translator died in 1936. Tanzil distributes its translation files 'for non-commercial purposes only' and asks other users to obtain permission from the translator or publisher.
sources.credit: English translation: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain. Text file from Tanzil (https://tanzil.net/trans/).
sources.notes: Downloaded from https://tanzil.net/trans/?transID=en.pickthall&type=txt-2. Kept verbatim in data/tanzil/en.pickthall.txt; data/quran.json copies each line unchanged. Tanzil's changelog lists one later fix (14 Sep 2010) although the file header still reads September 4, 2010. Tanzil asks for a link back to https://tanzil.net/trans/ when more than three of its translations are used; this project uses two and links back anyway.

sources.title: English Transliteration, Tanzil file en.transliteration
sources.license: Tanzil translation terms only: 'for non-commercial purposes only'. No translator or publisher is named (the file lists the translator as 'English Transliteration'), so permission for any other use cannot be requested. Not clearly redistributable beyond non-commercial use.
sources.credit: Transliteration: Tanzil Project, en.transliteration (https://tanzil.net/trans/), non-commercial use.
sources.notes: Interim choice, pending the owner's decision (see REVIEW.md). Kept because it is the only pinned, verifiable transliteration available to freeze: the Quran Foundation API may not be cached or bundled, and generating a transliteration from the Arabic would be machine-made scripture text that nobody has checked. It may be used only while the project stays non-commercial; replace it or obtain clear permission before any commercial use. Downloaded from https://tanzil.net/trans/?transID=en.transliteration&type=txt-2 and kept verbatim in data/tanzil/en.transliteration.txt. The file marks long vowels and silent letters with inline HTML (<u>, <b>, <i>, <strong>); data/quran.json removes those tags and changes nothing else, and scripts/validate.ts checks that.

sources.title: Planck PR3 (2018) SMICA CMB map, COM_CMB_IQU-smica_2048_R3.00_full.fits
sources.author: ESA and the Planck Collaboration
sources.license: Public data from the ESA Planck Legacy Archive, free to use with acknowledgement. ESA asks users to include: 'Based on observations obtained with Planck (http://www.esa.int/Planck), an ESA science mission with instruments and contributions directly funded by ESA Member States, NASA, and Canada.'
sources.notes: Mirror: https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/Planck/release_3/all-sky-maps/maps/component-maps/cmb/COM_CMB_IQU-smica_2048_R3.00_full.fits (2,013,312,960 bytes, last modified 2018-06-04). The HEALPix temperature map is converted offline into the equirectangular textures described by public/assets/cmb/cmb.json. ESA's own image pages for this map print the credit as 'ESA/Planck Collaboration'; this project uses the spec's wording 'ESA and the Planck Collaboration'.
